quote: And then Kellina, please please tell me Kellina. It's not Michelina. Okay?
stewart_read: A minor stumble handled well — rep asks her to repeat it and adjusts immediately, and the customer doesn't hold onto it.
coaching_implication: No action needed; this is a clean recovery worth noting as a positive example of quick repair.

quote: No. We cut a lot of them.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers that trees blocking sun were removed and the roof is new and in full sun — a strong qualification signal (better solar yield, no roof-age DQ risk) that the rep logs mechanically instead of reflecting back.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to verbally acknowledge signals like this ('that's great news for your system's output') — costs nothing and builds the customer's own case for solar before the closer call.

quote: Only requirement is that you have a credit score above 6 170.
stewart_read: The schema's credit threshold is 670; the rep's phrasing ('6 170') is garbled and ambiguous on the call, echoing prior drift the schema already flags from another rep who stated 650. This is a second data point suggesting the threshold isn't being stated cleanly/consistently across the floor.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be a transcription artifact of '670' rather than a rep error, but the ambiguity itself is a coaching-worthy clarity issue regardless of cause.
coaching_implication: Flag for reconciliation per the schema's drift-tracking note — confirm with Kenny whether 670 is still the active number and drill reps to state it as one clean number, not a run-together phrase.

stewart_read: Customer gives an average bill figure and the rep immediately moves to the next question ('would this be your first time looking at solar') without acknowledging or flipping the number into emotional leverage.
coaching_implication: This is the bill anchor moment — coach the rep to pause and reflect the number back ('$280 a month, that's real money going straight to the utility') before moving on.

quote: if you just wanna forward that over to my email, I can text you my email.
stewart_read: Rep offers his own personal email as the bill-collection channel instead of a company-controlled intake path, mirroring the schema's flagged anti-pattern for personal-contact bill collection (previously documented for personal phone numbers) — same privacy/scale-exposure concern.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as resourceful improvisation under friction rather than a violation, since Ion apparently lacks a formal automated bill-capture tool today.
coaching_implication: Flag for the floor's privacy/security review per the schema's roadmap note; until an automated capture tool exists this is the current workaround, but should be tracked as an anti-pattern to migrate away from.

quote: what we'll do is we'll set up, a meeting. So it'll actually just be, like, a phone call meeting, and then we'll have a specialist give you a call.
stewart_read: Rep describes the next step only in the abstract — no day, no time, no one-hour block, no 'is that fair' handshake — and the call ends without ever circling back to lock a date.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be deferring scheduling until the bill is in hand, consistent with the paid-lead requirement that the bill be captured before booking. But the schema's own guidance is that the setter should still lock a callback time even when bill collection is pending — that step was skipped entirely.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always lock a concrete callback day/time before hanging up, even when the bill isn't captured yet — 'I'll call you back Thursday at 2 once you've sent that over' costs nothing and protects the appointment from going cold.

quote: Okay. So maybe I'll if I get online, maybe I'll get that information without having to call them. I'll look.
stewart_read: Customer is still trying to help at the very end of the call, but the rep lets her leave with an open-ended 'I'll look' rather than converting her willingness into a specific, time-bound next step.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to convert this kind of customer-initiated effort into a firm commitment: 'Great — I'll call you back tomorrow at [time] once you've had a chance to check.'
